stories.title: FBI flash alert says Artex tool automating cyberattacks at ‘machine speed’
stories.reason: FBI flash alert: Artex AI-agent pentest framework automates intrusions machine-speed, 1600+ exposed consoles, privileged access in <3h, tied to Chinese state actors and ConnectWise supply-chain attack. Exactly the AI x cyber headline this feed exists for.
key_facts: Censys found 1,600+ publicly exposed Artex console instances
FBI says some intrusions reached privileged access in under 3 hours
Artex pairs with Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, Grok, Kimi; DeepSeek dominates attacker-controlled instances
Microsoft says Chinese state-backed actors used it in a ConnectWise supply-chain attack
Targets: financial services, government, tech, defense, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, telecom, legal

stories.title: Chinese frontier AI models carry the fingerprint of export-controlled GPUs
stories.reason: Researchers fingerprint which GPU class (Hopper vs Blackwell) initialized a model's weights purely from published open weights, showing several 2026 Chinese frontier models (DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K3, MiniMax-M3) were trained on export-controlled Blackwell GPUs -- novel verifiable methodology with strong statistical backing, not a rumor.
key_facts: Method: PyTorch's seeded RNG weight init reveals SM count, hence GPU class, from untouched weights
DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro, Kimi K3/K3.1-Pro, MiniMax-M3, Ant's Ling-3.1-flash read as Blackwell (148-152 SMs)
Statistical strength: 49-1385 sigma vs an ~8 sigma chance baseline across ~6e12 seed/layout combos
Matched all 24 models with publicly disclosed hardware; validated bit-for-bit on H100/B300/GB200
Cannot prove ownership, location, or export-rule violation -- only which GPU class initialized the weights

stories.title: Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer
stories.reason: Edge0-145B: open-weight 145B-param model (10B active) running on a single consumer laptop (~29GB), beating Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's six-benchmark mean (72.8 vs 71.7) at a fraction of the memory -- a genuine open-weight, on-device inference result with published weights.
key_facts: 145B total params, ~10B active per step; weights on HF (Edge0/Edge0-145B-NVFP4)
Runs at ~29GB peak memory on a MacBook Pro-class laptop; 80+ tok/s decode, 1100+ tok/s prefill
Six-benchmark mean 72.8 vs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's 71.7 (which needs ~70GB at 4-bit)
Benchmarks are vendor-reported/self-evaluated, not independently verified

stories.title: OpenAI disbands its robotics team as its general models start running robots
stories.reason: OpenAI disbands its dedicated robotics team, folding it into general research after finding frontier models like GPT-6 Astra (74.8% vs 51.0% for best specialized robotics models on an Nvidia benchmark) can directly control robots -- a real technical/organizational inflection, not just reshuffling.
key_facts: GPT-6 Astra-powered agent: 74.8% success on a simulated manipulation benchmark vs 51.0% for best specialized robotics models (Nvidia study)
Robotics research team folded into main research org (CRO Mark Chen); applied/hardware teams moved under Greg Brockman
Comes amid reported $10.9B quarterly operating loss and a planned funding round/possible 2027 IPO

stories.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0 : A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem
stories.reason: llama.cpp reaches v1.0.0 with a stable, semver-versioned public C API (libllama/libggml), 150+ architectures supported, ~10 distribution channels -- a real inference-infra stability milestone, not a feature announcement.
key_facts: libllama and libggml both reach v1.0.0 with public headers and semver guarantees
Supports 150+ model architectures plus mainstream speculative decoding methods
Distributed via ~10 channels: prebuilt binaries, Docker, Debian, Homebrew, conda-forge, Winget, XCFramework
Project is about 3.5 years old

stories.title: CapLite: Prompt-Injection Defense for Small Language Model Agents without Model-Written Security Artifacts
stories.reason: CapLite defends small LLM agents from prompt injection without the model writing its own security policy -- zero successful attacks across 13,935 AgentDojo episodes at 18% of CaMeL's token cost, beating prior enforcement defenses on 15 open models -- strong empirical AI x cyber result, though no code repo is linked (bare-ish arxiv paper, docked per Learned rule on unlinked arxiv work).
key_facts: Derives write policy from tool schemas; no model-written security artifact needed
Zero successful attacks across 13,935 attacked AgentDojo episodes
Utility under attack: 29.0% vs 27.2% for CaMeL, using ~18% of CaMeL's tokens (17.1k/episode)
On 15 open-weight models (13 between 1.7B-12B), prior defenses (Progent/IPIGuard/DRIFT) were broken on 11-14 of them
No linked code repository found on the arxiv page
